property_summary: After any successful transferFrom of a minted position id to a nonzero recipient `to`, the position's owner must equal `to`; the mutant instead leaves/sets ownership to `from`, breaking the rule for any `to != from`.

After a successful transferFrom of a position to a recipient, the recipient owns it and can transfer it onward without any prior approval; the mutant leaves ownership with the original owner so the recipient's onward transfer reverts.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,uint256): recipient must be able to retransfer the received position

property_summary: After any authorized transferFrom of a minted position to a nonzero recipient, the token's owner becomes the recipient (ownerOf(id)==to); the mutant never updates _ownerOf, so ownership stays with the previous owner for some transfer.

Whenever an order is filled, the taker (msg.sender) must become the owner of the newly minted opposite-position token (ownerOf(positionId) == msg.sender, never the zero address); the mutant assigns address(0) on mint, so ownerOf(positionId) reverts/returns zero for some fuzzed order.

For every admissible order, a successful fillOrder must record the taker as owner of the minted opposite-order position (ownerOf(positionId) == taker); the mutant never writes _ownerOf on mint, so ownerOf reverts NOT_MINTED for some fill.
For any token id that has never been minted, ownerOf(id) must fail (no owner recorded); the mutant keeps stale ownership records so some id ends up with a recorded owner when it should have none.

Burning (transferring to the dead address) must fully erase ownership: for any actor and any token id, either the transfer-to-burn call reverts or, afterwards, ownerOf(id) must revert (no owner may remain recorded); the mutant keeps the stale owner in _ownerOf, so after a completed burn ownerOf(id) still returns the previous owner and the rule fails.
